entries.contractRationale: The first-account and cached-clock finding remains a real safety defect, but K01/K02 move its target to a scoped discovery descriptor and a provider-declared market-session observation instead of a shared execution interface.

entries.contractRationale: The safe $1 GTC scenario and Ack/query/cancel evidence are retained, while the former generic SDK boundary is replaced by three exact leaf schemas and an optional transaction wrapper only around mutation.

The final cancel/cleanup is outside the place plan, so it is a separate authorized cleanup transaction (Manual|PolicyApprovalBinding) with its own PreparedPlanRecord/ApprovedPlan and durable DispatchStarted; no direct adapter bypass.

entries.contractRationale: Positive quote observations remain useful evidence, but K05 requires treating them as data delivery rather than an order transaction; K03 makes units and freshness schema-bound instead of numeric assertions.

Keep quote data read-only and separate from order dispatch.

Make market-open requirement a precondition result rather than a module bool.
verificationCases: A stale quote cannot authorize a price-derived order.
A missing bid with a valid last is accepted only for a market order, not for a spread assertion.

entries.contractRationale: The source proves place acknowledgement followed by a later Filled/position observation, not a universal lifecycle API. The target keeps before-image, Ack-versus-observation, and operation-owned delta while letting the Alpaca adapter declare its exact request/result/error schema.

entries.problem: Immediate place success and a later Filled observation are conflated; the second buy depends on test ordering and has no baseline or per-operation scope.
entries.targetModel: Alpaca market-order placement is an effect leaf composed with withTransaction for a real-account controlled effect; fill and position checks are separate order-observation and position-read leaves keyed by operation scope. Cleanup is not part of this source slice; the adjacent position-close scenario owns any later cleanup.

A timeout remains Unknown and forbids blind retry. Any later position close belongs to the separate MAP-D684830A67 cleanup operation and needs its own authorization/identity.
preservedBehavior: Preserve returned order-ID logging and fill-polling intent; the later position read remains an observation, not a fill or cleanup receipt.
Do not infer cleanup from this source slice; the adjacent position-close scenario owns any later cleanup as a separate operation.

Persist poll deadline and last observed cursor for restart-safe reconciliation.
verificationCases: PreparationPreview cannot create a remote market order; approval produces ApprovedPlan{binding,queuedJobs} and queues work before DispatchStarted.
A successful Ack followed by timeout remains Unknown and does not issue a duplicate market buy.
Confirmed Filled quantity creates exactly one scoped position delta; any cleanup must be a separately authorized operation bounded by its own observed delta.

entries.contractRationale: The source close-all call is retained as evidence of an available behavior, but K04/K08 require its exposure policy and ownership to be explicit rather than inheriting a global close contract or prior test state.

entries.targetModel: Alpaca position.close is a provider effect leaf with explicit ExactQuantity or AllExposure input, scope and InstrumentId; withTransaction is applied only when the close is a controlled remote effect.

Stop treating a prior test as the owner of current exposure.

Add operation-owned before/after exposure records and keep generic AllExposure only when capability/policy allows.

A partial close observation larger than the operation delta is rejected for compensation.

entries.contractRationale: The batch lookup remains worthwhile data evidence, while cleanup moves into its own controlled effect boundary. This prevents read absence from acquiring approval semantics and preserves durable idempotency only for the actual cleanup write.
entries.currentBehavior: A further market buy waits, queries getOrders([id]), and closes the position; the suite uses IDs and status but no durable receipt.
entries.problem: Batch query is not scope-bound and cleanup after an ambiguous result can be duplicated or target the wrong order.
entries.targetModel: Alpaca order.query is an Account-scoped finite pull leaf with cursor/completeness variants; any follow-up cancel/close is a separate effect leaf composed with withTransaction and operation-owned OrderRef/PositionDelta.

Preserve remote IDs without assuming they imply filled state.
replacementSteps: Replace direct array query with typed scoped query and an authorized durable cleanup job.
Use idempotency/lease keys for retries and retain RecoveryRequired when observation is ambiguous.
verificationCases: An unapproved cleanup has no remote effect; approval queues one cleanup job and two retries of the same job produce one remote effect or an explicit Unknown, never two closes.
Batch query containing another scope is rejected before projection.

entries.contractRationale: The ID-substring and first-match defect is retained, but the target now derives a Bybit discovery descriptor and availability evidence without requiring every provider to expose the same provider methods.

Pass RuntimeAccount/AccountScope through every scenario.

Two demo accounts require an explicit selector and do not silently choose first.

entries.contractRationale: The source account/position/search observations remain valuable; K03/K04 reframe them as exact provider leaf schemas rather than a loose loose adapter result, while K05 keeps reads outside order transactions.

Remove symbol-only position keys from projections.

Spot ETH/USDT and ETH/USDT:USDT produce distinct InstrumentIds, and a perpetual position missing settle currency is not projected as valid.

entries.contractRationale: The raw Exchange call is a genuine source fact and the S7 diagnostic exception is preserved, but K07/K08 require separate read, external-stimulus, and ordinary effect contracts so the raw probe cannot become a second UTA authority.

S7 takeover/cancel is a separate authorized cleanup transaction (Manual|PolicyApprovalBinding) with its own durable identity; failed or out-of-bound recovery enters RecoveryCase.

An S7 external order is observed with actor/provenance and is not counted as a UTA dispatch; failed takeover/cleanup remains RecoveryRequired.
A diagnostic invocation without either a read-only capability or explicit S7 external-stimulus authorization cannot mutate the account.

entries.contractRationale: The 0.01 close remains a useful scenario when owned exposure exists, while K04/K08 remove implicit prior-buy ownership and confine durable cleanup guarantees to the controlled close effect.

Preserve reduce-only semantics for the perp.

Replace previous-test dependence with explicit scenario context and durable order observation.

Unknown close result enters RecoveryRequired with an observation job.

entries.contractRationale: The five-second wait is correctly replaced by durable observation, but K01/K07 keep the adapter free to expose its native order fields and error schema rather than forcing a universal lifecycle implementation.

entries.targetModel: Bybit market order placement is a provider effect leaf composed with withTransaction; Ack, order observation, and position observation are distinct typed leaves/jobs with cursor and deadline data.

entries.contractRationale: The Decimal/tick and parent-linked-leg obligations remain, but the old optional TPSL object becomes a precise provider extension and capability/availability result under K02-K04; the empirical bracket question is therefore still open.

Without a venue capability/observation fixture proving parent-linked TP/SL legs, the outcome remains BracketCapabilityAbsent or BracketObservationUnknown and cannot be recorded as bracket-confirmed.

A crash after trigger Ack schedules observation/cancel, not duplicate trigger creation; unknown external cleanup remains RecoveryRequired.

entries.contractRationale: The source proves dummy credentials are used only to reach a public catalog endpoint. K01/K02/K07 preserve the public-read possibility and move secret resolution to the adapter boundary without claiming a provider-wide initialization guarantee.

entries.contractRationale: Spot/swap visibility is retained as a catalog fact, while the count threshold is removed as a contract. K03-K05 make completeness and identity declaration-driven and keep catalog reads separate from order effects.

entries.contractRationale: The observed mark-price fallback remains worth preserving with provenance, but K03/K04 prevent a fallback or currency from being silently promoted to a universal executable fact.

pureTransitions: valuePosition(q,p) -> Money using Decimal and explicit rounding

entries.contractRationale: BTC/ETH perpetual discovery remains the source obligation. K02-K04 put venue/product identity in the leaf schema and keep catalog observations independent from controlled writes.

pureTransitions: attach Public scope and catalog version

Preserve CRYPTO_PERP semantic requirement.

Reject prepared plans compiled against a changed catalog.

ETH absence returns a typed NotFound/Blocked disposition, not a passing skip.

entries.contractRationale: The 0.001 BTC scenario and its missing-finality/currency evidence are retained, but K03/K07/K08 prevent a source comment or Ack from becoming a universal fill or USD guarantee.
entries.currentBehavior: Places a 0.001 BTC perp market buy, expects success/orderId, optionally validates execution, then reads BTC position and USD normalization.
entries.problem: Success and optional execution do not distinguish Ack from fill; the source comment about a $10 minimum is not runtime proof, and the later position read can race while USDC-to-USD normalization lacks an explicit policy.
entries.targetModel: Hyperliquid market order placement is an effect leaf composed with withTransaction; minimum-notional/lot constraints, Ack, execution observation, position read, and stablecoin normalization are separate typed capabilities.
entries.effectBoundary: Market search/place/position calls, withTransaction writer/approval, and queue submission are effects; only an approved queued plan reaches the Hyperliquid adapter, while plan validation and currency policy are pure.
entries.durability: JournalWriter commits Prepared plan, approval binding, queued DispatchStarted, ack, observation, and position snapshot; no fill assertion from Ack alone and no remote mutation before approval.
preservedBehavior: Preserve the 0.001 BTC test quantity only when the declared venue minimum-notional/lot capability accepts it; do not treat the source comment as a universal guarantee.
Preserve optional execution logging without requiring it when the venue omits it.
replacementSteps: Make minimum notional a capability/precondition using Decimal price and require withTransaction authorization/queueing.
Route position verification through scoped observation reconciliation.
verificationCases: PreparationPreview or missing approval has no remote effect; approval queues the plan before DispatchStarted, and an Ack without execution and without a confirming position observation remains Unknown.
Missing quote/constraint evidence blocks admission; confirmed fill with USDC maps to USD only under an explicit versioned policy.

For an account mode or execution-latency path without observed finality and currency-policy evidence, preserve ExecutionUnknown or CurrencyNormalizationUnavailable rather than claiming a fill or USD equivalence.
openQuestions: The source does not prove Hyperliquid execution/fill latency or stablecoin normalization across all account modes; live acceptance must supply observed execution and currency-policy evidence.

entries.contractRationale: The source has a standalone reduce-only BTC close test and a separate buy/query/close test; K08 requires each remote write to have explicit authorization, with the standalone close treated as cleanup rather than inheriting a later buy's approval.
entries.currentBehavior: The source first runs a standalone reduce-only BTC close, then in a separate test buys, waits three seconds, queries Filled, and closes again.
entries.problem: Reduce-only and cleanup are not represented as typed intent; fixed waits and sequential test state make duplicate/over-close possible, and the standalone close has no operation-owned baseline.
entries.targetModel: Hyperliquid order.place and position.close are separate provider effect leaves. The standalone initial close is an explicitly scoped authorized cleanup operation; the later buy/query close uses an operation-owned delta and may use an approved compensation allowance only when that allowance is bound to the same buy.
entries.effectBoundary: Remote calls/timers, withTransaction writer/approval, and queue submission are scheduler effects; only approved buy/close plans reach the Hyperliquid adapter, while close validation and status transition are pure.
entries.durability: JournalWriter persists a prepared, separately authorized cleanup plan for the standalone close; the later buy and its operation-owned close persist their own Prepared/approval/queued steps before DispatchStarted. Durable idempotency and observation jobs survive crash, and Unknown prevents blind redispatch/over-close.
preservedBehavior: Preserve reduceOnly standalone cleanup and Filled query expectation.
Preserve cleanup after the second buy only when its owned delta is observed and authorized.
replacementSteps: Replace waits with leased observation jobs and before-image.
Bind every approved order/close to AccountScope and InstrumentId and retain operation-owned delta.
verificationCases: PreparationPreview cannot mutate; approval queues no operation until binding exists, and external exposure change makes a requested close exceed owned delta and blocks it.
Crash after approved dispatch resumes status observation without duplicate buy.

entries.contractRationale: The demo-only intent remains, but K02/K07 make environment and availability evidence explicit and avoid requiring a generic provider surface for all providers.
entries.currentBehavior: Setup chooses the first CCXT account whose id contains okx and exposes generic broker; prose requires demo preset but code does not verify it.
entries.problem: Code can accidentally run against live OKX despite documentation, and ID matching is ambiguous.
entries.targetModel: OKX runtime discovery yields a verified Demo RuntimeAccount with scope, endpoint evidence, readiness epoch, and declared capabilities; prose or ID substrings are not authority.
entries.effectBoundary: Preset/config read and provider initialization are effects; environment policy is pure.
entries.durability: Persist verified environment/scope; reject mutation if demo evidence is absent.
preservedBehavior: Preserve demo-only intent and the provider capability adapter.
Preserve an explicit NotReady/Blocked disposition when no OKX account is available; it is not a passing live mutation result.
replacementSteps: Replace id substring/index with preset/environment resolver.
Feed scope into all spot and derivative actions.
verificationCases: An OKX account with preset mode `live` never reaches placeOrder.
Two demo accounts require deterministic explicit selection.

entries.contractRationale: The source-specific spot synthesis and product distinction remain important. K03-K05 keep this as typed read composition and do not spread order approval or compensation into balance/position reads.
entries.currentBehavior: Account requires USD base currency and positive equity; positions combine derivative positions and synthesized spot holdings, requiring currency/positive market price/value≈quantity×price.
entries.problem: Spot holdings and derivative exposure have different identities and valuation provenance, while the source also asserts positive equity even though zero or negative signed equity is a valid account observation; one loose Position shape hides both distinctions.
entries.targetModel: OKX account.read and position.read are account-scoped pull leaves that retain separate SpotHolding and DerivativePosition schemas, settlement/currency, valuation provenance, and signed account facts.
entries.effectBoundary: fetchPositions/fetchBalance/market data are adapter effects; merge and valuation are pure.
entries.durability: Persist source/provenance and catalog version; never merge spot/perp IDs.
preservedBehavior: Preserve derivative + spot synthesis and the value invariant.
Preserve USD normalization only when adapter policy proves it; retain zero or negative reported equity/cash as signed facts for risk policy rather than rejecting the account.
replacementSteps: Split adapter records before domain projection; add product kind and valuation source.
Use currency/unit parsers instead of Number coercion.
verificationCases: BTC/USDT spot and BTC/USDT:USDT perp remain separate positions, and a zero/negative account equity read is retained as SignedMoney rather than discarded.
A balance with no mark price is not emitted as a positive-valued position.

entries.contractRationale: The exact spot/perp coverage is retained as a query requirement, while K04 removes local-symbol equality as a universal identity and K05 keeps search outside trading transactions.
entries.currentBehavior: BTC search requires exact spot and perp local symbols; ETH search requires exact perp symbol.
entries.problem: Exact local-symbol strings are venue-specific and bypass canonical product identity/catalog version; this public instrument search must not fabricate an account scope.
entries.targetModel: OKX instrument.search is a Public or provider-declared catalog pull leaf with base/quote/product/settlement filters, catalog revision, and explicit Unique|Ambiguous|NotFound resolution; localSymbol is native evidence.
entries.effectBoundary: Market search/load is IO; query resolution is pure.
entries.durability: Persist selected InstrumentId and catalog version as evidence input to a later controlled effect; search remains a finite read without transaction state.
preservedBehavior: Preserve BTC spot+perp and ETH perp coverage.
Preserve human-readable local symbols in evidence.
replacementSteps: Replace localSymbol equality with canonical descriptors and explicit product filters.
Invalidate plans when mapping changes.
verificationCases: An ETH spot-only result fails an ETH perp query with ProductTypeMismatch.
A changed settlement suffix does not alias an existing InstrumentId.

entries.contractRationale: The source separates a $50 buy and a sell-back test; K04/K08 retain exact notional/valuation/dust facts but the sell-back must not inherit an approval from a different test or silently consume pre-existing spot.
entries.currentBehavior: Spot buy uses cashQty=$50, waits for balance, expects synthesized long with positive value and zero PnL; a separate sell-back test sells the entire observed BTC spot quantity and permits dust below 10%.
entries.problem: Notional sizing, balance propagation, synthetic avg cost, dust threshold, and cleanup are implicit; sell can touch pre-existing BTC.
entries.targetModel: OKX spot order.place and spot order.close are effect leaves with Notional/Units input, provider lot/tick/minimum constraints, operation-owned AcquiredDelta, and a declared ResidualPolicy; withTransaction wraps each write, and the sell-back uses a separate cleanup authorization unless both writes are explicitly modeled in one effect plan.
entries.effectBoundary: Quote, withTransaction writer/approval, queue submission, place, balance, and position reads are effects; notional conversion, dust comparison, and cleanup decision are pure.
entries.durability: JournalWriter commits the buy's Prepared quote/time, before balance, approval, queued order ref, DispatchStarted, after balance, and cleanup result. Because the source sell-back is a separate test, the default target treats it as a distinct authorized cleanup transaction with its own identity; it may sell only an operation-owned delta captured in that transaction, and residual or out-of-bound cleanup enters RecoveryCase. No false zero position if dust remains.
preservedBehavior: Preserve the $50 spot buy and an explicitly authorized sell-back with a declared dust policy.
Preserve zero unrealized PnL for synthetic cost basis, but label it Unknown rather than economic truth.
replacementSteps: Add notional ADT and venue minimum/tick capability; route the approved plan through withTransaction writer/queue.
Compute operation-owned acquired quantity and sell only that delta.
verificationCases: PreparationPreview or missing approval has no remote effect; approval queues the $50 notional order before DispatchStarted.
A pre-existing BTC holding remains after selling the approved test delta.
Balance delay yields StillWorking/Unknown and does not issue another buy; dust below threshold is recorded as residual and policy outcome.
When account-specific dust/minimum-balance evidence is unavailable, the residual remains policy-unknown/RecoveryRequired rather than being classified by a universal percentage.
openQuestions: The exact OKX dust/minimum-balance threshold is venue/account dependent; retain policy configuration and observe residual rather than hard-code a universal threshold.

entries.contractRationale: The observed 51010 classification is retained, while K02/K03/K07 require conservative adapter decoding and keep unmapped codes as provider rejection/unknown until evidence exists.
entries.currentBehavior: Perp helper detects OKX code 51010/current-account-mode by regex and returns `{orderId,cashMode}` for callers.
entries.problem: Regex over error strings is unstable and a boolean helper conflates capability refusal with transport/domain failure.
entries.targetModel: OKX order.place exposes a provider-declared error schema including the observed AccountModeUnsupported variant; capability availability is a leaf decision, not a global ProviderError map or boolean cashMode flag.
entries.effectBoundary: Adapter parses raw OKX error; pure capability policy returns typed decision; no account mode mutation implicit.
entries.durability: Persist capability observation and refusal, not raw credentials/error payload.
preservedBehavior: Preserve cash-mode non-trading behavior and code 51010 handling.
Preserve orderId when a perp order succeeds.
replacementSteps: Implement typed OKX error decoder in adapter; expose capability result.
Remove `cashMode:boolean` API and map callers exhaustively.
verificationCases: A 51010 response produces AccountModeUnsupported and no retry.
A different error text/code remains ProviderRejected and is not silently skipped.
Only the observed 51010/current-account-mode evidence may produce AccountModeUnsupported; an unmapped account-mode code remains ProviderRejected or Unknown until adapter evidence classifies it.
openQuestions: The adapter must empirically map OKX account-mode error codes beyond the observed 51010 text before classifying additional variants as non-fatal capability refusal.

entries.contractRationale: The source’s contextual Cash-mode and 51205 branches remain, but K02/K07 prohibit a blanket skip and K08 limits durable approval/recovery to actual derivative writes.
entries.currentBehavior: ETH perp buy/position/close skips on Cash mode, mode error, or absent position; close recognizes code 51205/reduce-only unavailable.
entries.problem: Multiple unrelated error strings are treated as test skips, hiding unknown failures and not preserving mode/position state.
entries.targetModel: OKX derivative order.place and position.close are separate effect leaves composed with withTransaction; account-mode refusal, NoExposure, provider rejection, and unknown observation are distinct result/error variants.
entries.effectBoundary: Adapter decodes codes; withTransaction writer/approval, queue submission, and provider mutations are effects, while scenario/classification records typed Blocked/NoExposure dispositions or enters recovery, never a blanket skip.
entries.durability: JournalWriter commits Prepared plan and approval binding before queued/DispatchStarted mutation; scope-bound refusal/NoExposure observations are durable and Unknown blocks completion; mode is not auto-switched. This standalone close is a separate authorized cleanup transaction (Manual|PolicyApprovalBinding), and any ambiguous or out-of-bound recovery remains in RecoveryCase.
preservedBehavior: Preserve the explicit Cash-mode and genuinely contextual no-exposure handling; a missing ETH perp in tryPerpBuy remains a typed NotFound/precondition failure, not a blanket skip.
Preserve reduceOnly close requirement and never auto-switch account mode.
replacementSteps: Replace regex/mode/empty skip branches with exhaustive error ADT and an explicit withTransaction approval/queue path.
Keep account mode unchanged; do not auto-switch it.
verificationCases: Cash mode, 51205 with contextual no exposure, or missing approval has no remote effect; the same code without exposure context is not accepted.
A missing market or malformed error is NotFound/Unknown and enters recovery, not a passing skip.

entries.contractRationale: The fixed wait and helper identity are real defects; the target keeps Ack/fill/position distinctions and restart-safe observation without asserting a universal order lifecycle.
entries.currentBehavior: Derivative helper buys ETH perp, waits three seconds, getOrder expects Filled, then searches and closes 0.01.
entries.problem: Fixed delay and helper-derived identity lack durable observation, baseline, and idempotent cleanup.
entries.targetModel: OKX derivative order.place and position.close are provider effect leaves with exact reduce-only/native extensions; durable observation and operation delta are composed by withTransaction only for the remote writes.
entries.effectBoundary: OKX place/get/search/close and timing plus withTransaction writer/approval/queue submission are effects; only approved plans reach the adapter, while transitions/classification are pure.
entries.durability: JournalWriter commits Prepared plan, approval binding, queued attempt/observation/close jobs, and scope-bound IDs; DispatchStarted precedes entry mutation and no duplicate dispatch occurs after crash. The operation-owned reduce-only close reuses the original ApprovedPlan CompensationAllowance{class,target,riskBudget} and durable step identity without a new approval; an unknown or out-of-bound delta remains RecoveryRequired.
preservedBehavior: Preserve order query Filled assertion when returned by venue.
Preserve final reduce-only cleanup.
replacementSteps: Use scheduler observation rather than sleep and require withTransaction authorization/queueing; persist canonical perp ID.
Close only the operation delta.
verificationCases: PreparationPreview creates no remote order; approval queues the plan and worker restart after approved place resumes getOrder by remote ID.
If order is Filled but position query is delayed, keep Reconciling rather than buying again.

entries.contractRationale: The source any-cast exposes a mutation-capable Exchange, so K07 requires a named adapter diagnostic boundary and K02 requires availability/authorization to be explicit while preserving the excluded diagnostic lane.
entries.currentBehavior: Diagnostic setup selects a Bybit account, exposes `(broker as any).exchange`, and skips if absent.
entries.problem: A private Exchange instance and any-cast are used as a separate mutation-capable authority.
entries.targetModel: Bybit diagnostic context is a scoped capability-discovery/read view. A direct mutation is only the explicitly authorized S7 ExternalStimulus leaf; it is not an ordinary UTA order leaf or second generic execution authority.
entries.effectBoundary: Account lookup/init is effectful; diagnostic authorization and context construction are pure.
entries.durability: Read diagnostics are append-only evidence tied to run/scope. An S7 external order records its external actor/provenance and native identity for UTA observation/takeover; it is not a UTA transaction receipt.
preservedBehavior: Preserve the deliberately excluded Bybit diagnostic as a typed NotReady/Blocked disposition when no account is available.
Preserve the S7 direct-probe exception only as external stimulus with separate evidence; it cannot bypass Alice/UTA for takeover or be counted as UTA execution.
replacementSteps: Remove the untyped Exchange escape hatch from ordinary UTA code; expose a named adapter diagnostic/probe interface.
Keep the diagnostic command outside the aggregate paper sweep and route any S7 observation/takeover/cancel through the scoped UTA path.
verificationCases: A diagnostic read returns normalized redacted order metadata without exposing SDK objects.
An authorized S7 external order is visible to UTA as ExternalStimulus and can be taken over/cancelled through Alice; an unauthorized diagnostic mutation is denied.

entries.contractRationale: Selected response fields and cleanup intent remain evidence, but K03/K07/K08 remove raw info persistence, swallowed cleanup errors, and any implicit third execution authority.
entries.currentBehavior: Raw createOrder logs many normalized fields plus `info`, then best-effort reduce-only close catches and discards errors.
entries.problem: Raw createOrder logs selected fields plus info, then a reduce-only cleanup failure is swallowed; this loses cleanup Unknown and, unless explicitly marked as S7 external stimulus, bypasses transaction authority and redaction.
entries.targetModel: Raw CCXT response inspection is a redacted diagnostic read leaf; if S7 creates an order, that creation is an ExternalStimulus effect with actor/provenance/native reference, while normal mutation uses a provider order leaf plus withTransaction.
pureTransitions: classifyCleanup(error) -> CleanupOutcome, with no swallowed failure or empty catch
entries.effectBoundary: Only the adapter/probe performs the raw SDK call; withTransaction writer/approval/queue submission, redaction, and outcome classification are boundary effects, and S7 takeover/cancel is executed by UTA rather than the probe.
entries.durability: For normal UTA mutation, JournalWriter persists Prepared plan, approval binding, queued DispatchStarted/receipt, and durable cleanup. For the S7 exception, record external actor/provenance and native identity before observation; evidence does not pretend a UTA dispatch occurred, and cleanup uncertainty creates RecoveryRequired.
preservedBehavior: Preserve selected diagnostic fields (id/status/symbol/fill/cost) only in safe redacted form.
Preserve the deliberately excluded external-stimulus probe and cleanup intent, but surface failure and route takeover/cancel through Alice.
replacementSteps: Make raw diagnostics read-only by default; retain direct order creation only under explicit S7 external-stimulus authorization or route normal mutation through withTransaction/queue.
Replace raw info logging and empty catch with typed redacted outcome and effect-owned observation/cleanup.
verificationCases: A normal unapproved mutation has no remote call; a response containing private fields is redacted or rejected before evidence persistence.
A failed S7 external-stimulus cleanup creates a RecoveryRequired record with native identity rather than passing or silently retrying.

entries.contractRationale: The source’s diagnostic visibility remains useful, while K05 makes pagination and absence data semantics explicit and prevents a read result from authorizing a retry or cleanup write.
entries.currentBehavior: Diagnostic fetches closed/open raw orders and logs id/status/symbol/amount without substantive assertions.
entries.problem: Unscoped raw order reads cannot distinguish account scope or pagination completeness and are not useful durable evidence.
entries.targetModel: CCXT order history/open-order inspection is an Account-scoped finite pull leaf with cursor, namespace, completeness, and redacted OrderObservation records; absence is Found|NotFoundWithEvidence|Unavailable, not rejection.
entries.effectBoundary: fetchClosedOrders/fetchOpenOrders are adapter effects; pagination/normalization/completeness are pure.
entries.durability: Persist only redacted query evidence if retained; query snapshots are not transaction confirmations.
preservedBehavior: Preserve diagnostic visibility of IDs/status/symbol/amount.
Do not turn logs into success assertions.
replacementSteps: Introduce typed paginated query and scope binding.
Keep raw diagnostic suite out of production workflow and avoid SDK types in shared domain.
verificationCases: A page lacking cursor metadata is marked incomplete.
An order from another account/scope is rejected from the evidence set.

entries.contractRationale: Spot/perp comparison and the optional probe remain valuable, but K02/K05/K07 separate incomplete catalog data from mutation and forbid absence or partial pages from authorizing an order.
entries.currentBehavior: Diagnostic checks spot/perp market presence, creates raw perp/optional spot orders, prints IDs/errors, and best-effort closes.
entries.problem: Optional spot mutation and raw presence checks mix catalog diagnosis with account mutation; raw errors are strings and the source is an external probe, not a UTA dispatch.
entries.targetModel: CCXT catalog probing is a read-only instrument.list/search capability with Public or provider-declared scope and NamespaceCoverage. Any retained direct order is a separate S7 ExternalStimulus effect whose observation/takeover is not a catalog result.
pureTransitions: no implicit fallback from probe to UTA execution
entries.effectBoundary: Market map/order calls are adapter effects; policy/classification are pure and redacted.
entries.durability: Persist capability results/catalog version. An S7 order is an external-stimulus evidence record, not a UTA dispatch; UTA observation/takeover/cancel owns subsequent transaction receipts and cleanup.
preservedBehavior: Preserve spot/perp comparison and optional spot diagnosis as a separately labeled external probe.
Preserve IDs/errors as safe summaries and surface unknown cleanup.
replacementSteps: Separate read-only product probe from the S7 external-order scenario; remove direct raw calls from ordinary UTA execution.
Model optional spot as an explicit capability branch and route takeover/cancel through Alice with RecoveryRequired on uncertainty.
verificationCases: Spot unavailable yields ProductUnavailable without attempting an unauthorized probe.
An authorized S7 external order with unknown outcome blocks cleanup and remains visible as external stimulus.
Until paginated spot/perp namespace and cursor coverage are evidenced as complete, the catalog probe remains Partial or Unavailable and cannot authorize mutation or absence conclusions.
openQuestions: The diagnostic source does not establish complete spot/perp namespace coverage; catalog probe must report Partial/Unavailable until adapter pagination evidence exists.

entries.contractRationale: Native metadata visibility and spot/perp distinction are retained. K03/K04 ensure the record is a data descriptor and never a hand-written symbol routing or global order variant.
entries.currentBehavior: Logs market.id, symbol, type, and settle for ETH/USDT candidates.
entries.problem: Native IDs and symbols are logged without canonical identity or catalog version, encouraging symbol-based routing; the public catalog evidence must not be mistaken for an account fact.
entries.targetModel: CCXT instrument metadata is a Public catalog pull leaf returning canonical InstrumentId plus exact native id/symbol/type/settlement evidence, product-aware currency, and catalog revision.
pureTransitions: compareProducts uses InstrumentId and product-aware currency rules
entries.effectBoundary: loadMarkets is adapter IO; identity mapping is pure.
entries.durability: Persist catalog snapshot/hash and mapping evidence; native fields never become cross-layer identity by themselves.
preservedBehavior: Preserve visibility of native market id/symbol/type/settle.
Preserve distinction between spot and perpetual.
replacementSteps: Expose canonical catalog query; keep native fields inside adapter/evidence.
Require InstrumentId for later intents.
verificationCases: Two native records with the same canonical product identity but conflicting currency metadata are rejected.
A valid spot descriptor may omit derivative settleCurrency when quote currency is explicit; a perpetual descriptor without settle currency is non-executable.

entries.contractRationale: The all-versus-since comparison and external visibility probe remain, while K05/K07 distinguish query absence from mutation and preserve cleanup uncertainty without blind redispatch.
entries.currentBehavior: Compares unbounded and since-filtered closed orders, places an order, checks whether it appears within ten seconds, and best-effort closes.
entries.problem: Temporal query completeness and not-found semantics are unknown; absence after an external probe is not rejection, and the swallowed reduce-only cleanup error hides residual risk.
entries.targetModel: CCXT closed-order history is an Account-scoped finite cursor pull leaf with Found|NotFoundYet|Unknown completeness outcomes. The deliberate S7 placement/cleanup is a separate ExternalStimulus effect and any takeover/cancel uses withTransaction.
entries.effectBoundary: Clock, order query, placement, and cleanup are effects; cursor/deadline classification is pure.
entries.durability: Persist query cursor and external-stimulus provenance/native identity; UTA observation/takeover/cancel receipts remain authoritative. Never blind-redispatch from a missing closed-order result.
preservedBehavior: Preserve comparison of all vs recent history and the excluded external placement visibility probe.
Preserve cleanup intent only with surfaced Confirmed|StillWorking|Unknown|Rejected outcome; unknown requires recovery.
replacementSteps: Use provider observation leaf with bounded cursor/status namespace and explicit ExternalStimulus evidence.
Replace string match logging and empty catch with typed outcome, UTA takeover/cancel, and durable evidence.
verificationCases: An external order absent from a partial page is NotFoundYet, not rejected.
After a complete-history deadline, classify unresolved identity as Unknown and require recovery review rather than retrying or passing.

entries.contractRationale: The source already refuses unsafe cleanup; K02/K03/K07 retain that boundary as a typed leaf-specific identity error rather than a generic thrown exception or universal order handler.
entries.currentBehavior: requiredOrderId throws when an open order has no orderId, explicitly preventing unsafe cleanup.
entries.problem: Throwing generic Error loses a domain distinction: missing remote identity means cleanup cannot prove which order to cancel.
entries.targetModel: RemoteOrderRef is a refined provider observation value carrying AccountScope; an order without a usable remote identity yields MissingRemoteOrderId and blocks destructive cleanup. No approval machinery is attached to this pure identity check.
entries.effectBoundary: Open-order query is an effect; identity refinement and cleanup decision are pure.
entries.durability: Record the observation and blocked cleanup atomically; if cleanup is an in-flight effect, enter RecoveryRequired rather than silently continuing.
preservedBehavior: Preserve refusal to continue unsafe cleanup.
Preserve remote ID when present.
replacementSteps: Replace throw helper with domain Result/typed failure crossing adapter boundary.
Require all IBKR cleanup paths to handle the variant exhaustively.
verificationCases: Open order with undefined ID leaves baseline/cleanup unresolved and no cancel is sent.
A valid ID allows idempotent cancel observation.

entries.contractRationale: The first-account and cached clock defects remain, but K01/K02/K07 keep TWS protocol details provider-native and make readiness/availability distinct from order execution state.
entries.currentBehavior: Setup picks the first IBKR account, initializes broker, reads market clock, and stores marketOpen.
entries.problem: First-match account selection and cached session state are not explicit scope/readiness evidence.
entries.targetModel: IBKR runtime discovery is a TWS/Gateway-backed capability descriptor with scope, Paper environment, endpoint/readiness epoch, and fresh MarketSession observation; limit and market leaves query their own session needs.
entries.effectBoundary: TWS/Gateway connection, account config, and clock are effects; pure gate sees only typed observations.
entries.durability: Persist endpoint readiness/scope and session observation before any dispatch; no credentials in evidence.
preservedBehavior: Preserve paper TWS/Gateway and market-hours split.
Preserve provider adapter isolation.
replacementSteps: Replace first IBKR account/global bool with explicit runtime descriptor.
Re-read session at market mutation boundary.
verificationCases: A closed session refuses market order but permits safe limit lifecycle.
A TWS reconnect does not imply prior transaction recovery.

entries.contractRationale: The source conId and Decimal observations remain required, while K03/K04 prevent native Contract objects from becoming the shared UTA type and K05 keeps reads outside order transactions.
entries.currentBehavior: Connectivity reads account/cash/clock, searches AAPL, gets Contract details, and checks Decimal quantity/string position fields.
entries.problem: Native Contract details and account/position values are not normalized into canonical identity, scope, and unit-qualified fields.
entries.targetModel: IBKR account.read and position.read are account-scoped pull leaves; instrument.search/detail may be Public or account-scoped according to its declared schema. Canonical InstrumentId/conId evidence, signed money, Decimal quantity, and valuation completeness are explicit fields.
entries.effectBoundary: TWS requests and native SDK decoding are adapter effects; canonical parsing/validation pure.
entries.durability: Persist catalog version and observations; native conId is retained as identity evidence, not leaked SDK object.
preservedBehavior: Preserve AAPL search/conId and Decimal/string invariants.

Preserve account/position observations without treating the source positive-equity assertion as a universal validity rule; signed zero/negative equity remains queryable while risk admission rejects nonpositive denominators.
replacementSteps: Map native Contract through an adapter decoder; move typed snapshots to domain.
Bind reads to AccountScope.
verificationCases: A non-positive conId cannot produce an executable InstrumentId.
Decimal quantity and serialized Money survive round trip without IEEE noise; a parsed negative equity is retained as a signed observation.

entries.contractRationale: Currency equality and no-position behavior remain worthwhile source constraints. K03 turns them into leaf schema validation and K05 prevents read validation from acquiring order approval semantics.
entries.currentBehavior: Account baseCurrency must be a nonempty string; each position currency must exist and match contract.currency when present.
entries.problem: String checks do not encode currency units or missing/ambiguous contract currency.
entries.targetModel: IBKR account.read and position.read are account-scoped leaves carrying refined CurrencyCode/Money and explicit currency-source variants; a missing position is absence of an account data item, not a fabricated currency.
entries.effectBoundary: Account/position reads are effects; currency parsing/invariant is pure.
entries.durability: Persist currency in each observation and include it in conflict keys; no silent currency default.
preservedBehavior: Preserve currency field and contract equality requirement.
Preserve no-position early return.

Require explicit FX source when converting.
verificationCases: A position in CHF against USD contract yields CurrencyMismatch.
Absent positions do not fabricate currency observations.

entries.contractRationale: The polluted-field/no-state-delta experiment remains a strong read/what-if obligation. K05 separates it from cleanup, while K07/K08 preserve durable scoped cleanup only when a real remote effect is detected.

entries.problem: Identity/routing safety and baseline cleanup are implemented by ad-hoc finally logic; what-if result, no-state-delta, and evidence have no durable transaction relation.

Preserve exact baseline order IDs/position comparison and cleanup of only introduced orders.

Make cleanup a durable scoped job and record evidence after commit.

Polluted symbol/secType/exchange cannot override conId.

entries.contractRationale: The safe non-filling GTC path and missing-ID guard remain, but K01/K02/K07 replace a generic native order lifecycle with exact leaf schemas and preserve WAL/idempotency only for writes.

entries.effectBoundary: TWS operations/timers, withTransaction writer/approval, and queue submission are effects; only approved plans reach the IBKR adapter, while state transition and query merge are pure.

The final cleanup is outside the original limit plan, so it is a separate authorized cleanup transaction (Manual|PolicyApprovalBinding) with its own durable DispatchStarted; unknown or missing identity enters RecoveryCase.

Preserve GTC semantics.

Remove ad-hoc finally as sole safety mechanism and preserve GTC semantics.

Batch query cannot return another scope and cancel is sent once per idempotency key.

entries.contractRationale: The observed timeout tolerance and unknown-error failure remain, while K03/K05 keep market-data availability in a data capability and do not couple it to order approval or a closed SDK.
entries.currentBehavior: AAPL snapshot quote requires positive last/bid/ask; a known TWS snapshot timeout is logged and skipped, other errors rethrow.

Preserve rethrow/stop for unknown errors.

Record the blocked outcome in evidence instead of console-only skip.

A stale snapshot cannot satisfy FreshQuote.
A TWS/Gateway version or timeout variant not covered by the known decoder remains Unavailable or Unexpected and blocks FreshQuote; it cannot become a passing skip.

entries.contractRationale: The source’s exact baseline/positive-delta compensation is retained, but K08 limits WAL/CAS/lease/recovery to these remote effects and K01/K07 leave native order identity semantics to the IBKR adapter.

Replace finally-only cleanup with durable job/state transitions.

entries.contractRationale: The compact source record and privacy boundary remain, while K02/K03/K07 replace optional free strings with a declared evidence schema and make external stimulus distinct from UTA effect evidence.

Keep compatibility importer at evidence boundary, never as runtime authority.

entries.contractRationale: Environment/run/git precedence and the unknown fallback remain exact source behavior. K03/K07 keep provenance a typed evidence leaf rather than a secret or order-authority field.

Preserve unknown fallback as explicit unknown, not a guessed hash.

Unknown git commit never passes a FreshCodeVersion requirement.

entries.contractRationale: All copied native fields remain useful audit evidence, but K03/K04/K07 require canonical identity and exact native extension data without leaking the foreign SDK into UTA-facing contracts.

Version mapping and invalidate stale plans.

Missing conId for a product that requires it is non-executable, not silently symbol-routed.

Preserve returned path for operator evidence.

Never let evidence append determine transaction success.

A line claiming paper=true while verified environment is live is rejected/mismatched.

Concurrent writers serialize sequence allocation per run/sink key; same-sequence same-digest replay is idempotent, divergent payloads yield EvidenceConflict, and unavailable ordering never changes authoritative transaction state.

entries.contractRationale: The source TestAccount fields remain useful display/filter data, but K01/K02/K07 add the missing scope/readiness contract without turning IBKR/CCXT/Alpaca into one mandatory handler set.

Preserve a capability-handle reference at the adapter edge.

Make all scenarios consume AccountScope.
verificationCases: A single wallet still receives an explicit subAccountId.
An account descriptor without verified environment is not admissible for mutation.

entries.contractRationale: The engine-specific credential schemes and paper hints remain, but K03/K07 replace raw Records and boolean credential checks with schema parsing and provider-specific verification without claiming credential presence proves safety.

Add verified endpoint/account evidence before scenario admission.

IBKR without reachable TWS is NotReady despite no API key.

entries.contractRationale: The bounded TCP probe and false-safe behavior remain, while K02/K07 keep it as availability evidence and forbid an open socket from implying a complete provider capability or authenticated account.

Preserve false-safe behavior.

Inject host/port from secret/config references without writing credentials.

Timeout yields NotReady with reason and no provider initialization mutation.

entries.contractRationale: The 30-second bound and late-settlement guard are retained as lifecycle evidence. K01/K07 keep timer/cancellation/fencing implementation free while requiring only the typed readiness result at the UTA boundary.

Preserve per-provider isolation.

Ensure late provider completion cannot publish stale readiness.

Failure of one account does not erase other ready accounts.

entries.contractRationale: The source singleton optimization can remain test-local, but K01/K02/K07 distinguish cache availability from capability identity and prevent it from making a provider-wide capability contract or recovery decision.

pureTransitions: pure callers receive handles by scope

entries.durability: Initialization/readiness has run-scoped identity and lease; journal and provider effect state do not rely on process memory.

Preserve single init per test run as an optimization only.

Never use module cache to answer transaction recovery.
verificationCases: A new run gets a new readiness epoch.
A stale handle cannot dispatch after lease expiry.

entries.contractRationale: The per-account filtering, probe, timeout, and isolation facts remain, but K01/K02/K07 move construction/init errors into typed discovery evidence without requiring all providers to implement the same handlers.

entries.targetModel: DiscoveryResult{ready,skipped,observedAt,configVersion} is a typed runtime discovery capability. Each provider may implement its own factory/probe, while the UTA-facing result records scope, environment, capability availability, and exact failure variants.
pureTransitions: no ready fallback when an account is skipped; policy can require all/selected

entries.durability: Persist discovery snapshot/readiness before any action; selected account must match scope/config version, and skipped accounts remain auditable.

Preserve one account failure not blocking unrelated accounts when policy allows, including construction failures represented as typed skips.

Make selection policy explicit and bind result to run/account scope/config version.

A constructor or init failure for one account is recorded while another ready account remains selectable.
If policy requires a named account and it is skipped, scenario is NotReady, not redirected.

entries.contractRationale: Provider-engine filtering remains one useful dimension, but K01/K02/K07 reject index-zero ambiguity and make capability availability a query result rather than a generic provider assumption.

Preserve easy test selection for a unique configured engine.

Remove array `[0]` callers or make uniqueness checked.

A capability-missing account is returned as an explicit diagnostic.

entries.contractRationale: The source UTA setup and waitForConnect behavior remain as compatibility evidence, while K01/K02/K07 remove first-account/global state and keep runtime readiness separate from any order effect wrapper.

Preserve the existing UnifiedTradingAccount compatibility facade during cutover, without making it the provider contract.

Bridge push to durable transaction dispatcher.

Session closes after staging but before push causes precondition re-evaluation, not silent dispatch.

entries.contractRationale: The visible stage/commit/push/cancel flow and GTC non-fill remain, but K01/K07 separate Git projection, read queries, and provider-native mutation while K08 retains durability only for writes.

The explicit cancel command is outside the original place plan, so it is a separate authorized cleanup transaction (Manual|PolicyApprovalBinding) with its own durable identity; Git projection never authorizes it.

Preserve safe GTC non-fill.

Map each stage/commit/push to transaction commands/events, require approval before queueing, retain Git projection for user compatibility, and add durable cancellation observation.

entries.contractRationale: The source regression proves raw Function/Record and aliceId stamping are unsafe. K01-K05 replace casts with exact read schemas and keep all manager/provider reads outside order approval or compensation.

Each request declares Public or Account scope; AliceRef is parsed for account-bound routes into scope plus InstrumentId, and each result/error schema is provider-declared with no order state.

Preserve eventual position close.

entries.contractRationale: The source’s +1 and baseline restoration remain valuable, but K05 excludes the position/quote reads from transaction machinery and K08 keeps approval/compensation only around actual writes.

Preserve market-hours gate.

Keep UTA facade over transaction runtime during migration.

entries.contractRationale: ETH-perp discovery and account-qualified display remain, while K01/K02/K03 remove raw concatenation and preserve provider-native localSymbol only as evidence.
